submission.justification: This recommendation is provisional. It holds only if Sensor-T1 is shown to meet the radiation requirement. On resolution, Sensor-T1 is best at every thickness I simulated. It reaches about 5.7 um at 150 um. Results near the optimum are noisy (5.9-5.95 um at 100-175 um). Sensor-T2 is about 8.7 um and Sensor-T3 about 14.0 um at 150 um, which matches the 2025 summary. Important caveat: the hard requirement is at least 97% hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2. No project document and no available tool gives any irradiated or efficiency data for any candidate, because the simulation only covers unirradiated sensors. So I could not check the hard constraint for any option, Sensor-T1 included. Before this choice is approved, irradiated test-beam or TCAD efficiency data at 2e16 neq/cm^2 must be obtained. A sensor with fine pitch and strong charge sharing may lose efficiency after heavy irradiation, because the collected charge drops. If Sensor-T1 fails, the fallback should be whichever candidate the irradiated data shows passing. 3D-electrode sensors (Sensor-T3) are generally the most radiation-hard option at this fluence.

requirements.evidence: Simulated (unirradiated, 1e5 events): Sensor-T1 is 5.69 um at 150 um, 5.89 at 100, 7.38 at 50 and 8.14 at 300. Sensor-T2 is 8.72 at 150 and 9.76 at 50. Sensor-T3 is 14.0 at 150 and 16.05 at 50. Sensor-T1 at about 150 um is the best of everything simulated. This is for unirradiated sensors only.
